messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing increased pod->pod latency and RDMA handshake timeouts in eu-west1 GPU pool after the Calico 3.29 canary rolled at ~02:05 UTC. Jobs are failing with intermittent ETIMEDOUT on connect. Rolling back canary?

deploy-bot: calico canary deploy completed: calico/3.29 -> eu-west1-canary at 02:05:12 UTC

eric: I captured traces from a failed run. Lots of retransmits and out-of-order fragments. Example logs: `rdma_connect() failed: ETIMEDOUT`, `QP timeout waiting for response`. Link: https://internal.corp/trace/2101234567

ryan: do we have node MTU and tunnel mode info? suspect encap + SR-IOV mismatch. Can you paste `ip link` + calico Felix config from a canary node?

maya: pasted below from node eu-canary-05: ```
2: ens5f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
3: vf0@ens5f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default
```
And calico config snippet from `calico-config`:
```yaml
spec:
  veth_mtu: 1400
  tunnelMode: "geneve"
  tunnelMTU: 1400
```
Also tcpdump snippet from inside pod showing IP fragments: `IP (frag 1/2) 10.10.0.5 > 10.10.0.12: proto 113`

anita: That veth_mtu/tunnelMTU combo + host VF mtu mismatch is a red flag. We had SR-IOV VFs at 1500, host set 9000 earlier for RDMA but calico geneve added ~50 byte overhead -> inner packets are exceeding path MTU and getting fragmented/dropped when passed through the VF. RDMA/IB expects MTU alignment.

eric: tried a quick rollback to calico 3.28 on eu-canary-05 and eu-canary-06 — control plane went back but we still see residual fragment queues for a minute and some handshakes still time out until endpoints renegotiate. Rolling nodes seems to clear faster.

ryan: immediate mitigations: 1) Set calico veth_mtu to 9000 if using host NICs and SR-IOV (only safe if underlying fabric supports jumbo). 2) Or change tunnelMode -> "none" / disable encapsulation for this tier while we patch. 3) If rollback, drain+reboot nodes to flush stale path MTU state.

maya: trying option 2 on a single canary node: patching ConfigMap `felixConfigSpec.vethMtu=9000` and `tunnelMode=none` on eu-canary-07, will report back.

anita: opening incident (INC-2101) — marking eu-west1 GPU capacity as degraded, moving non-critical batch runs to west2 and tagging customers affected. @sre-bot please start capacity autoscaler to make room in fallback region. :warning:

sre-bot: Autoscaler triggered for west2-gpu-pool (scale +6 nodes). Estimated warm-up 7m.

maya: after disabling encapsulation on eu-canary-07, RDMA handshakes recovered for jobs run on that node, latency tails dropped back to baseline. tcpdump shows no fragmentation. Looks like encapsulation toggled default in 3.29 and didn't respect our SR-IOV assumptions.

eric: next steps: 1) block full rollout of 3.29 in eu-west1, 2) coordinate a patch for Felix to keep veth/tunnel MTU aligned with VF MTU, 3) add a preflight check in our upgrade playbook to validate VF MTU vs calico tunnelMTU. I'll file a PR with repro steps + tcpdumps.

ryan: agree. Also add a probe to the canary job that runs a small RDMA handshake workload for 30s post-upgrade. If it fails, auto-rollback.

anita: noted for postmortem and runbook update. tagging infra-eng on the ticket. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — holding eu-west1 rollout and draining remaining canaries. Will update ticket and slack thread when we have a full rollback or patched release scheduled.

maya: (followup) ETA for rollback complete on the cluster is 02:25 UTC, moving remaining jobs to west2 until patch is validated.
